concern.concern: The Statement defines a positive Hopf band solely as 'an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number +1.' This omits the unknotted-core condition. A framed annulus around a nontrivial knot can satisfy this linking condition. Knotting the b-annulus away from the plumbing square and the specified disk for a⁺ preserves the stated linking/intersection conditions and matrix calculation, but does not justify the trefoil boundary identification in Proof 1.1. The later word 'standard' needs an explicit restriction consistent with the initial definition. The conventional missing condition is explicit in Quach Hongler–Weber, §2, printed p. 137: [The link of an extrovert divide](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2000_6_9_1_133_0.pdf). Thus the definition and trefoil identification appear overbroad as written, although the displayed matrix follows from the other specified conditions.

original_concerns.reason: Linking of the induced annulus boundaries fixes its framing, not its knot type. A tubular annulus with nontrivial core and this framing meets the written definition. Local knotting of the second annulus away from the plumbing square and the first push-off disk does not change the given framing/intersection/linking conditions. Proof1.1, in contrast, uses the actual standard disk-and-three-band model; that geometric identification does not follow for these more general annuli. Add the missing unknotted-core condition for the conventional trefoil assertion and retain the original matrix-only result for all annuli satisfying the original hypotheses, since Proof2.1 depends only on those data.
